delivery.subsections: Use h3/h4 inside the five meaningful h2 groups; do not create additional top-level sections.
delivery.advancedDetail: Use labelled details blocks with reader depths. Every main group has an overview and optional depth; preserve requested reference material.

general: Choose one primary paper type by reader goal/outcome, then satisfy its required semantic coverage within at most five main groups.
Informational research opens with questions/scope and findings, not an invented problem, investment ask or default recommendation.
Decision-oriented papers explain the problem/context before the proposal and solution.
Every paper defines the actual terminology, distinctions and limits readers need. A definition is not evidence of agreement or implementation.
Every main group has useful overview content. Persona selection changes reading depth, never permissions, authority, evidence or result meanings.
Use Overview, Product/delivery and Technical/evidence reader levels. Let readers expand individual sections regardless of the global choice.

Collapse advanced code, full inventories, detailed data, optional scenarios and deep evidence. Do not hide material risks, unsupported claims, critical limits, recommendation conditions or scope exclusions.
Keep the core narrative concise. Requested implementation/reference detail may remain in collapsible subsections; do not conceal an oversized argument to game the budget.
Preserve exact authored facts, quotations, citations, IDs/deep anchors and prior versions during regrouping.
Cite sources actually read; distinguish documented, reported, verified, inferred, proposed and unresolved statements.
Never invent executed experiments, delivery, stakeholder agreement, owners, staffing, baselines, numeric targets or official event dates.
Use internal discussions as context, not meeting chronology or vague authority in the argument. Preserve decision-relevant versions and evidence limits.
Keep synthetic UI/data labelled. Selections, checkboxes, what-if models and readiness examples never approve, deploy or modify real systems.
Use the shared self-contained HTML templates and tested controls. No Markdown replacement, remote assets, live data calls, iframes or external form actions.
Only verified HTTPS source links and in-document anchors belong in durable papers. Never link to local files or copy secrets/private unrelated context.

Themes may change colors, offline system fonts, spacing and placement through CSS; preserve the HTML structure, content, reading order, mobile fit/pinch/pan, keyboard access, print readability and default/reader preferences.
Publish only on an explicit current-turn request. Template selection, paper approval, prior receipts and reader controls are not publication or external-write authority.
Prepare a coherent bounded decision or conclusion and an honest source boundary. Keep unconfirmed commitments labelled.
Explicit current user outline/citation requirements are respected without abandoning the five-group, terminology or HTML standard.
Load additional topic-specific constraints only from the caller's supplied or authorized project context; do not turn one project's decisions into universal paper rules.
